title: Only leave the alternate screen after a session that actually dropped
head: 15aede4c67ef
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A real drop during the first 30 seconds or a short retry leaves the remote alternate screen armed
leads.consequence: An interactive SSH session can enter a remote editor/tmux immediately and lose the network before 30 seconds. The client returns 255, but this branch sends mouse/focus/cursor resets without 1049l. The reconnect message, subsequent retries and eventually the shell prompt appear on the still-active alternate screen; a later successful/fast retry also skips 1049l, so returning to the primary scrollback can require a manual terminal reset. The same thing occurs on a short 255 retry following an earlier long drop. The old unconditional disarm left that screen. This is a regression in the recovery case, not a claim that all short 255s connected.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus finding 3 (short drop / retry short drop stuck alternate screen); published

leads.summary: A slow connect/auth failure or long remote-command status 255 still emits an unpaired 1049l
leads.consequence: Elapsed time is not proof of an established session or alternate-screen entry. A connect timeout lasting 30 seconds exits 255 without any remote TUI; the wrapper sends 1049l, restoring the cursor to home or an earlier save in Herdr, potentially overwriting prior lines. Similarly `ssh host 'sleep 31; exit 255'` emits 1049l even though the wrapper correctly declines to reconnect because the invocation has a remote command. A long transport drop after an ordinary shell also still jumps. In tmux 3.5a an unpaired 1049l is neutral only before any prior alternate-screen save: after a previous alternate-screen visit its saved cursor can be restored even on the primary screen. A terminal-side state query or tracking is needed to avoid both wrong branches.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up 1 confirmed 255 after 30 s without a session (multi-address connect timeout, slow prompt then refusal) still sends unpaired 1049l, same as base at first exit; published as 'Unchanged from base' paragraph

leads.summary: A clean or non-255 exit with uncleared remote terminal state is no longer repaired
leads.consequence: The remote process can arm the alternate screen then die without cleanup while its shell continues and eventually exits 0 (or another non-255 status). The wrapper now leaves 1049 armed, so local prompt/output stays on the temporary screen, while the old helper reset it even after 0. A clean terminal process normally undoes its own mode change, but process kill or a shell/script emitting 1049h then exiting does not. This is separate from the short-duration case: rc alone cannot establish the terminal's state.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus finding 3 (non-255 exit with TUI left armed); published

leads.summary: The existing shell regression test fails on the pinned head and never exercises the new branches
leads.consequence: `test/shell` runs this file automatically (test/shell:8-13,25-27). Its first `0 255` plan insists on the old contiguous sequence containing 1049l before 25h, whereas the new implementation omits 1049l for fast failures and moves 25h before 1049l even on the long path. With set -e the test stops at that assertion and none of the long-drop/retry assertions execute; update the expected fast output and separately assert long-drop and retry 1049l emission/non-emission. Base test passes.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus finding 1 (existing test fails; sed patch misses >= 30); published

leads.summary: Two non-stacked open SSH alternate-screen fixes conflict with this change
leads.consequence: #8084 also edits the retry and disarm blocks but splits the helper, with a different retry predicate (`elapsed >=30` even for rc=0); #13116 changes the same `_ssh_disarm` block to query terminal state and adds a helper and query-specific test assertions. The compare API reports both diverged, not stacked; local git merge-file yields two conflict hunks with #8084 and one with #13116 in the production function. Their tests merge textually but #13116's tests expect its `_ssh_primary_screen` which this head does not define. Neither PR can be merged after this head without resolving production hunks and reconciling semantics/tests. #8084 itself updates the obsolete test from H4, but is not in this PR.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus finding 2 (#8084, #13116 conflict); #12456/#8927/#9946 not relevant; published

limits: Conflicting open PRs #8084 and #13116 have no unambiguous merged executable production file; tests on a manually chosen conflict resolution would test that choice rather than the proposed heads. Their unchanged baseline tests and fixtures were inspected instead.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the premise holds, and the change removes the stray cursor jump after ordinary `ssh` calls. One issue: the repository's existing test for this wrapper fails on this head. The trade-off, a stuck alternate screen in a few uncommon cases, is noted below. #8084 and #13116 change the same function.

**Verified:** terminal behaviour for an unpaired `CSI ? 1049 l` (sent while already on the normal screen):

| Terminal | Unpaired `1049l` | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Herdr 0.8.2, Ghostty 1.3.1, xterm 411, VTE 0.84.1 | restores the cursor; to home if nothing was saved | Herdr run headless; others from source (`Terminal.zig`, `charproc.c`/`cursor.c`, `vteseq.cc`) |
| tmux 3.7c | jumps back to where the pane's last `1049h` saved the cursor; harmless only before the pane's first full-screen program | run headless; `screen.c` 710-742 |
| foot 1.28.0, Alacritty 0.17.0, kitty 0.49.1 | ignored | source |

Head against base for plain `ssh -V`: base scrambles the output in Herdr, and in a tmux pane that has run a full-screen program before. Head is clean in both. The mouse, focus-reporting and cursor-visibility resets are still sent after every `ssh` whose output goes to a terminal, as in base, so the wrapper's original fix for escape junk on mouse moves stays in place.

**Description correction:** "foot and tmux ignore the reset" is true for foot but not for tmux 3.7c. There, after an earlier `nvim` or `less` in the same pane, an unpaired `1049l` moves the cursor back (rows read `AFTER-13`, `AFTER-24`). So the PR also fixes tmux panes, not only Herdr.

### The existing wrapper test fails on this head

`test/shell.d/ssh-reconnect-test.sh` line 97 still expects the old sequence, with `\e[?1049l` before `\e[?25h`:

```text
merge base: 17 of 17 ok
head:       10 ok, then
            not ok - stray terminal modes are reset after ssh exits
            (output: ...\e[?1004l\e[?25hrc=255)
```

The file stops at its first failure, so the 6 remaining assertions (reconnect, replay, stdin, Ctrl-C) do not run. The test is unchanged on the current `quattro`.

**Impact:** `./test/shell` fails for this file.

**Suggested change:** the test lowers the threshold with `sed 's/< 30/< 2/'` (lines 78 and 136). That does not touch the new `>= 30` checks, so dropping `1049l` from the expected string alone would pass without ever exercising the branch that sends `1049l` after a drop. A version that did check it:
- `sed 's/< 30/< 2/; s/>= 30/>= 2/'` on both lines.
- Check all three threshold markers (`started < 30`, `started >= 30`, `attempt >= 30`).
- Expect the new disarm sequence.
- Add four assertions: no `1049l` after a fast failure, none after a normal exit, exactly one (right after the disarm) for a dropped session that reconnects, and exactly one when the following retries fail fast.

That version passed 21 of 21 on the head, including the Ctrl-C test. It failed at the matching assertion for each of three mutants: always send `1049l`, never send it, and `||` instead of `&&` in the retry check.

### Where the alternate screen now stays on

A stub `ssh` entered the alternate screen like a remote TUI, then exited. Run in headless tmux 3.7c and Herdr 0.8.2:

| Exit of the ssh call | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `255` before 30 s | back on normal screen | stays on alternate screen |
| any non-`255` status | back on normal screen | stays on alternate screen |
| `255` after 30 s (tmux only) | back on normal screen | back on normal screen |

How these can happen:
- **Non-255 exit:** a remote tmux client or editor is killed or crashes without restoring the terminal, and the user then exits the remote shell normally.
- **255 within 30 s:** `~.` or a server reset shortly after connecting. A silent network loss does not count here: Omarchy's keepalive settings (15 s × 3) put its detection past 30 s.
- **Reconnect loop:** a retry that re-attaches a TUI and drops within 30 s, followed by Ctrl-C. Base had already left the alternate screen after that attempt; head has not.

All of these are much rarer than the old corruption. On the terminals that apply an unpaired `1049l` (see the table above), that corruption followed every `ssh` whose output went to a terminal, including `ssh -V`, failed connects and `fip`. `tput rmcup` recovers; inside tmux, `reset` does not leave the alternate screen.

**Impact:** the new code comment "Only a session that was established and then dropped can have left it armed" is stronger than the behaviour: a non-255 exit can leave the alternate screen on too.

**Suggested change:** soften that comment and name the trade-off in the PR description.

**Unchanged from base:** a 255 exit after 30 s with nothing on the alternate screen still sends an unpaired `1049l`. That covers a plain shell session that really drops, a connect that times out across several addresses (`ConnectTimeout` is per address), and a password or host-key prompt left for 30 s or more, then refused. The 255-plus-time check cannot tell these apart from a dropped TUI session. #8084 documents the dropped-session case; this PR does not.

### Overlap with #8084 and #13116

All three PRs rewrite `_ssh_disarm`, so only one can merge as is. Neither #12062 nor this PR mentions #8083 or #8084, which came first.

- **#8084** (opened 2026-08-24) takes the same approach and already updates the test. Run through the same stub `ssh` cases, 4 of 13 differ:
  - Head sends `1049l` when a remote-command or redirected-stdin session drops, for example `ssh -t host tmux attach`. #8084 sends none.
  - After a reconnected session runs past 30 s and exits normally, #8084 sends an extra unpaired `1049l` (its loop check ignores `rc`). Head does not.
- **#13116** asks the terminal whether the alternate screen is on (DECRQM) before sending `1049l`. When the terminal answers, that is the only one of the three that also avoids the unpaired case above; with no answer within 0.5 s it sends `1049l` anyway. It reads from the terminal. The side effects listed in its review thread were not re-checked here.

Related issues: #8083, #12062, #13057, and herdrdev/herdr#3602.

**Optional:** the first-session check reads `SECONDS` twice, once for `_ssh_disarm` and once for the reconnect `if`. `local dropped=$(( rc == 255 && SECONDS - started >= 30 ))`, used by both, would remove one duplicated `30` and a narrow window where the two reads disagree. The test markers would then need to match.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned head `15aede4c`, merge base and #8084's head `e5a394bf`. The repository test and the new test version were run in an isolated sandbox with a stub `ssh`; no real connection, network drop or `~.` was exercised. Most cases lower the 30 s threshold to 2 s as the repository test does; two used the unmodified file with real 28 s and 31 s sessions. Only tmux 3.7c and Herdr 0.8.2 were executed, headless; the other terminals and OpenSSH exit statuses come from reading source. The wrapper file and its test are unchanged on the current `quattro`.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
